### Count class initializers by shape: enums and their switch maps are all the apps have (Phase 4b)

change `wnxlynrsoosq` · [log `a1ad840061a3`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/63d80e44-36d9-4bcb-9e72-e31c6d9336ef/a1ad840061a3ae521eaa6e3b64061c8d56c6c8ecf831cb3c07c6ce18851245c2.jsonl.gz)

jvmcontract gaps now gives each class-initializer gap's &lt;clinit> a shape, read from its bytecode and the application methods it calls: enum, throws, other-statics (javac's $SwitchMap class for a switch over an enum), constants (literal tables only) or other, with traits. examples/tools/initializer_shapes.py runs that scan over the 59 recorded B9/B11 examples on the javac apps, writing no notes, and over each app with every method a target.

Count (JDK 25.0.5): the apps have 49 initializers, 36 enums and 13 switch maps over enums, and none that throws, assigns only constants or does anything else. Of the recorded examples only 013 and 071 reach initializers, the same four Quorum raft enums. The benchmark's only initializers are the conformance cases': Boom and Base throw through a helper, Quiet assigns a literal table. So Phase 5 takes full JVMS 5.5 semantics, starting with static fields as path state and initialization with ExceptionInInitializerError/NoClassDefFoundError (closing boom, inherited, quiet), then enums.

### Run application class initializers in the own checker, as JVMS 5.5 does (Phase 5, step 1)

change `kumppqkzlvwn` · [log `ed3d74a123ae`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/63d80e44-36d9-4bcb-9e72-e31c6d9336ef/ed3d74a123aed84a62f91bcf561108de42a68666d6fe064eb2f81acd2ae67265.jsonl.gz)

The own checker (lib/src/bmc) now keeps an application class's static fields as path state and runs its &lt;clinit> at the class's first new, getstatic, putstatic or invokestatic, after its superclass and the superinterfaces that declare a default method. A use from inside the class's own initialization goes on, an exception leaving an initializer becomes ExceptionInInitializerError (an Error stays as it is), and a later use of an erroneous class throws NoClassDefFoundError. An initializer outside the engine's fragment stays a named class-initializer gap (gaps::runs_initializer). Over the four apps that is still every one of the 49 initializers: enums, through $VALUES, an array of references, and their switch maps. The gap scan walks the initializers the engine runs and refuses static fields only of the JDK or of classes whose initializers don't run.

The interpreter that replays witnesses was fixed to match the JVM: erroneous classes and NoClassDefFoundError, Errors not wrapped, superinterface initialization, and getstatic/putstatic initializing the declaring class only. Verified on JDK 25.0.5. The conformance cases boom and inherited are now violations whose witnesses replay, and quiet is verified, in every native mode. 8 new cases (16 claims: static state, construction, superclass first, a cycle between initializers, the declaring class only, default-method interfaces, an Error thrown as is, NoClassDefFoundError) agree with the JVM in every mode. The conformance test still fails only its 12 pre-existing library-record claims, which come from the JDK mismatch. The unit (145), integration (64) and skill tests pass.

the_benchmark_takes_its_first_group_from_this_corpus now fails on this branch. lib/benchmark/conformance.json belongs to the JBMC stream, so the reconcile loop has to regenerate it with JVMCONTRACT_BLESS=1. The stream brief's Progress names every shared file changed.

A new test, the_models_only_jbmc_runs_agree_with_the_jvm, relocates the models out of java.* and runs the cases' calls on them against the JDK's own classes. They agree, and a mutated model fails it. ### Record the own checker's solver calls as replayable incremental CNF transcripts (Phase 6a)

change `wnktqxrtllpw` · [log `d4f4c0b4b794`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/63d80e44-36d9-4bcb-9e72-e31c6d9336ef/d4f4c0b4b7947cc26bd397dcbdbdd81fdf2254f3f0f4fe950f58d28c84c053db.jsonl.gz)

A check by the own checker can now write every clause it gives CaDiCaL and every call it makes, in order, as CaDiCaL's incremental CNF (p inccnf), each call followed by a comment with its answer, its time and its per-call limit, under a header naming the tool, the solver, the method and the engine's options. The new lib/src/bmc/transcript.rs writes and replays them. bmc::Options::transcript names a file; otherwise JVMCONTRACT_TRANSCRIPTS names a directory and each check writes PID-N.icnf there, which reaches prove, equivalence and the benchmark's runner without a flag. jvmcontract transcript FILE runs one again on the bundled CaDiCaL with the recorded limits and reports times and contradicting answers (exit 1). Phase 6c judges solvers on these sequences, since a check is hundreds of incremental calls with model-dependent lemmas between them.

### Put the own checker's SAT solver behind a narrow interface (Phase 6b)

change `syntvmqpxlzs` · [log `67fd094d3533`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/63d80e44-36d9-4bcb-9e72-e31c6d9336ef/67fd094d3533a2bd8208e5f575e30b9f41de9e11de317910beabcc2ab29abae6.jsonl.gz)

The own checker's solver is now reached only through a Sat trait (lib/src/bmc/sat.rs: signature, add_clause, set_limit, solve under assumptions, value, variables), with CaDiCaL 1.9.5 as the bundled crate gives it as its one implementation. That separates the engine's three layers: scheduling the queries (Engine in bmc/mod.rs: probes, deferred paths, the refinement loop), encoding them (Blaster in bmc/bits.rs, which now holds a Box&lt;dyn Sat> and calls nothing else of the solver), and solving them. bmc::Options::solver chooses the solver a check runs on (CaDiCaL by default), and transcript::replay_on replays a transcript on any solver behind the trait, so Phase 6c can put Bitwuzla's SAT mode behind it without touching the engine. The transcript's header now names the solver the check ran on. Results still name CaDiCaL through solver_signature(), since nothing outside tests sets another solver.

No behaviour changes. A new engine test runs a check on a test double that logs everything crossing the trait: it gives the plain run's outcome, its clauses and calls match the outcome's counts and the transcript's, and a replay on the logged solver gives the same clauses and calls again. End to end, held/lower-bound (equivalence --engine native, unwind 9, arrays up to 8) writes the same transcripts by count as before the change: 460 calls over 43,478 clauses and 13,025 variables, verified, plus a 5-call check, both replaying with no contradiction. Unit (153), integration (64) and skill tests pass. Conformance fails only its two known tests: 12 library-record claims (JDK 25.0.5 against a record made on 25.0.4.1) and the JBMC stream's benchmark file. The brief's Progress records this, the shared file changed (lib/README.md), and the next step: enums in the own checker.

- **The checker** (`lib/src/bmc/`):
  - Static fields of application classes are now tracked on each path.
  - A class's `<clinit>` runs at the class's first `new`, `getstatic`, `putstatic` or `invokestatic`. Its superclass and any superinterfaces with default methods are initialized first.
  - A use from inside the class's own initialization goes on without waiting for it.
  - An exception leaving an initializer becomes `ExceptionInInitializerError`, unless it is an `Error`, which is thrown unchanged. A later use of that class throws `NoClassDefFoundError`.
- **What stays a gap:** an initializer the checker can't run stays a named `class-initializer` gap (`gaps::runs_initializer`). In the four apps that is still all 49: the enums, because of `$VALUES` (an array of references, which the checker refuses), and their switch maps. Rerunning `initializer_shapes.py --apps-only` gives the same 49.
- **The gap scan** now walks the initializers the checker runs. It refuses a static field only when the field is the JDK's, or belongs to a class whose initializer doesn't run.
- **The interpreter** (shared file) was changed to match the JVM so that the checker's counterexamples replay correctly:
  - a class whose initialization threw is marked failed, and later uses throw `NoClassDefFoundError`;
  - an `Error` is no longer wrapped;

I committed Phase 6a as `wnktqxrt`. The own checker can now write every clause and solver call it makes to a file, and a new command runs that file again on CaDiCaL to check the answers.

- **How to use it:** set `JVMCONTRACT_TRANSCRIPTS` to a directory and every check writes one file there. `prove`, `equivalence` and the benchmark's runner pick it up without a flag, so Phase 6c needs no change to the other stream's benchmark code. `jvmcontract transcript FILE` replays a file on the bundled CaDiCaL with each call's recorded time limit. It reports the time against the recorded time, and exits 1 if an answer differs.
- **Format:** the files are CaDiCaL's own incremental CNF (`p inccnf`). After each call, a comment gives its answer, time and time limit.
- **Checked:**
  - Unit tests cover reading and replaying files.
  - An engine test shows a recorded check gives the same outcome as an unrecorded one, and its transcript replays with no differing answer.
